assumptions.name: N_OUTPUTS
assumptions.comment: ASSUMPTION: answers produced in one simulated period

assumptions.name: PERIOD_DAYS
assumptions.comment: ASSUMPTION: length of the simulated period (400 answers a day)

assumptions.name: ERROR_RATE
assumptions.comment: ASSUMPTION: share of answers that contain an injected error

assumptions.name: INJECTION_WEIGHT
assumptions.comment: ASSUMPTION: a failure type is injected in proportion to its likelihood score (1-5)

assumptions.name: BASE_CATCH
assumptions.comment: ASSUMPTION: chance a reviewer catches an error they look at, before modifiers

assumptions.name: FATIGUE_ONSET
assumptions.comment: ASSUMPTION: fatigue starts after this many consecutive clean items

assumptions.name: FATIGUE_FULL
assumptions.comment: ASSUMPTION: fatigue is at its maximum after this many consecutive clean items

assumptions.name: FATIGUE_MAX_DROP
assumptions.comment: ASSUMPTION: at full fatigue the catch chance falls by 35%

assumptions.name: TEAM_CAPACITY
assumptions.comment: ASSUMPTION: reviews the team can do in a day without loss of quality

assumptions.name: LOAD_DROP
assumptions.comment: ASSUMPTION: each extra team-capacity of daily reviews cuts the catch chance by 25%

assumptions.name: LOAD_FLOOR
assumptions.comment: ASSUMPTION: load never cuts the catch chance below half

assumptions.name: PLAUSIBLE_MULT
assumptions.comment: ASSUMPTION: catch chance is multiplied by 0.55 when the wrong output looks plausible

assumptions.name: PLAUSIBLE_BY_DETECTABILITY
assumptions.comment: ASSUMPTION: chance an error looks plausible, by the failure type's detectability score

assumptions.name: GUARDRAIL_STRENGTH
assumptions.comment: ASSUMPTION: scales how much the guardrail risk score separates errors from clean answers

assumptions.name: GUARDRAIL_SIGNAL
assumptions.comment: ASSUMPTION: mean risk-score shift for an error, by error type (clean answers score N(0,1)); planning errors look normal to most guardrails

assumptions.name: GUARDRAIL_SEVERITY_SLOPE
assumptions.comment: ASSUMPTION: extra risk-score shift per severity point

assumptions.name: MIN_PER_REVIEW
assumptions.comment: ASSUMPTION: reviewer time per answer

assumptions.name: DEFAULT_BUDGET
assumptions.comment: ASSUMPTION: current review budget

assumptions.name: SNOWBALL_HOUSEHOLDS
assumptions.comment: ASSUMPTION: households holding the fund with the stale price

assumptions.name: SNOWBALL_ANSWERS
assumptions.comment: ASSUMPTION: agent answers that use the stale price during the day

assumptions.name: SNOWBALL_DAY_MIN
assumptions.comment: ASSUMPTION: the trading day; answers arrive evenly at random through it, the stale feed starts at minute 0

assumptions.name: ROOT_CAUSE_CLUSTER
assumptions.comment: ASSUMPTION: risk-based review links the catches to the feed once this many answers with a freshness flag on the same fund have been reviewed

assumptions.name: INVESTIGATION_MIN
assumptions.comment: ASSUMPTION: time from the cluster to blocking further answers that use the feed

assumptions.name: QUALITY_DAYS
assumptions.comment: ASSUMPTION: length of the quality-monitoring window

assumptions.name: QUALITY_SLICE
assumptions.comment: ASSUMPTION: size of the daily random review slice used to estimate quality

assumptions.name: DRIFT_START_DAY
assumptions.comment: ASSUMPTION: the true error rate starts to rise on this day

assumptions.name: DRIFT_PER_DAY
assumptions.comment: ASSUMPTION: rise in the true error rate per day after drift starts

assumptions.name: ALERT_LIMIT
assumptions.comment: ASSUMPTION: alert limit on the estimated error rate

assumptions.name: ALERT_DAYS
assumptions.comment: OLD RULE, kept for comparison only: alert when the daily corrected estimate is above the limit this many days in a row

assumptions.name: MIN_CANARIES_FOR_ALERT
assumptions.comment: ASSUMPTION: warm-up; no alert can fire until at least this many canaries have been seen in total

assumptions.name: ALERT_WINDOW_DAYS
assumptions.comment: ASSUMPTION: trailing window for the alert estimate (the day and the days before it)

assumptions.name: ALERT_RULE
assumptions.comment: Alert on any day, after the warm-up, when the pooled corrected estimate is above ALERT_LIMIT: non-canary errors found / non-canary reviews over the trailing ALERT_WINDOW_DAYS days, divided by the cumulative sensitivity (canaries caught / seen to date), capped at 100%. Every alert day is recorded

assumptions.name: QUALITY_EVAL_RUNS
assumptions.comment: Monitor evaluation: the 14-day series is simulated this many times; per rule we report the share of runs with an alert before drift starts, the median days from drift start to the first alert on or after it (alert on the drift start day = 0 days), and the share of runs with no alert on or after drift start within the window

assumptions.name: BANNER_MULT
assumptions.comment: ASSUMPTION (reviewer experiment only): a coverage and freshness banner raises the catch chance by 25%

assumptions.name: ALERT_FATIGUE_MULT
assumptions.comment: ASSUMPTION (reviewer experiment only): alerts on 40% of items cut the catch chance by 40%

assumptions.name: EXPERIMENT_ITEMS
assumptions.comment: ASSUMPTION: planted errors shown per condition in the reviewer experiment

assumptions.name: EXPERIMENT_REVIEWERS
assumptions.comment: ASSUMPTION: reviewers in the reviewer experiment

assumptions.name: T1
assumptions.comment: ASSUMPTION: team-added failure mode 'Wrong tool selected' (Planning), not in the workbook; team-added, pending Lopa's review

assumptions.name: LOPA_MODES
assumptions.comment: Lopa's three priority failure modes

assumptions.name: MIN_INJECTED_PER_MODE
assumptions.comment: ASSUMPTION (strategy simulation only): each of Lopa's modes is oversampled to at least this many injected errors per run, by reassigning errors from the most common other failure types so the total stays the same. The quality series is not oversampled

assumptions.name: CANARY_PER_DAY
assumptions.comment: ASSUMPTION: known errors seeded into each day's random review slice, drawn from the natural error mix and reviewed like any other answer. More than the suite's 1 in 50 so the reviewer catch rate can be estimated, at the cost of fewer real answers reviewed

assumptions.name: CORRECTION_METHOD
assumptions.comment: Corrected error rate = errors found in the non-canary reviews / non-canary reviews, divided by reviewer sensitivity (canaries caught / canaries seen to date), capped at 100%. 95% interval: 2.5th-97.5th percentile of CORRECTION_DRAWS draws of Beta(found+1, misses+1) / Beta(canaries caught+1, canaries missed+1)

assumptions.name: CORRECTION_DRAWS
assumptions.comment: Monte Carlo draws for the corrected-estimate interval
